entities.name: Aulus Manlius Vulso
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aulus Manlius Vulso, a Roman senator, played a pivotal role in shaping the fate of ancient Italy. Born into a prominent aristocratic family, Vulso rose to prominence through his strategic alliances and military victories.

From 194 to 192 BC, he was a key member of a board tasked with colonizing the Thurii and Castrum Frentinum regions. This endeavor had a lasting impact on the region's geography and population.

In 178 BC, Vulso was elected consul, solidifying his position as a leading figure in Roman politics. His leadership during this period contributed significantly to the growth and expansion of Rome.

Vulso's legacy extends beyond his political accomplishments. His contributions to the development of Roman law and governance continue to influence modern legal systems.

The inscription on the Arch of Titus, which commemorates the conquest of Jerusalem, serves as a testament to Vulso's enduring impact on the Roman Empire.

As the Roman Empire expanded, Vulso's name became synonymous with bravery and strategic prowess.
